evidence: Mechanism is demonstrated, not just asserted. (a) 'Single signal cannot serve both pools': the language pool is decode-bound (ITL/token-throughput axis) while the vision pool's need is driven by image count/forwards -- distinct axes. EDA shows a constant-fraction (rate-proportional) model explains only R^2=0.123 of the image-rate series vs 0.654 of decode demand, and the two signals' top-percentile minutes are essentially disjoint, so no one signal captures both. (b) 'Signal invisible to reactive monitors': the vision failure (p99 encoder delay 5.0 s) arises from episodic FIFO queueing while mean utilization sits at 29% and the minute-mean stays low even as the 1-minute peak busy fraction reaches 0.90 -- so rate/mean-utilization/minute-averaged dashboards read healthy while the tail SLA is violated all day. The needed signal is the image-count series itself, which reactive monitors do not watch. 'Cannot' is strong but the underlying mechanism (axis mismatch + averaging blindness) is directly shown.
fix: 'Cannot' could be softened to 'does not' since the demonstration is against the specific monitored signals (rate, mean util); but the axis-mismatch argument makes the necessity defensible.
